Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register and then press the star key followed by the 1 key on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star 1 again. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 2024 results. With me on the call are Mike Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; and David Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mike Rivera.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities, including portfolio optimization, innovation, sustainability, digital transformation, and operational excellence.

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, sustainability initiatives, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $14.2 billion, representing a 7.2% increase compared to the prior year, or 8.1% on an organic basis—ahead of our guided range of 6-8%. This marks our sixth straight quarter of organic growth, driven by a healthy mix of 5.4% pricing actions and 2.7% volume/mix gains. Adjusted diluted earnings per share were $1.68, surpassing our guidance midpoint and up 12% from last year, reflecting strong gross margin expansion and disciplined SG&A control.

Gross profit reached $7.9 billion, yielding a gross margin of 55.6%, up 210 basis points year-over-year. This improvement stemmed from 220 basis points of supply chain efficiencies, including our resin and palm oil hedging programs that offset inflation in cocoa and transportation—challenges we've seen across the industry, much like Hershey and Mondelez. We also benefited from 90 basis points of favorable mix shift toward premium SKUs like Vitality+ organic snacks and EcoFresh household cleaners.

Adjusted operating income was $3.1 billion, delivering an operating margin of 21.8%, up 140 basis points, with SG&A steady at 19.2% of sales due to zero-based budgeting and AI-driven demand forecasting that cut promotional waste by 15% in North America.

By segment, Food & Beverage—52% of sales—grew organic sales 9.2%, led by 6.8% pricing and 2.4% volume, highlighted by Revive energy drinks gaining 18% market share in convenience channels per Nielsen and PlantPower plant-based yogurts adding 3 points of ACV in grocery. Household & Personal Care achieved 7.5% organic growth, driven by PureGlow shampoos in premiumization—now 25% of segment sales versus 18% last year—and eco-friendly wipes meeting EU plastic regs. Health & Wellness rounded out at 6.8%, boosted by ImmuBoost supplements with strong e-commerce uptake.

Regionally, North America—78% of sales—posted 9.4% organic growth, beating IRI CPG growth of 4.2%, with robust 7.1% pricing in club and mass channels. EMEA grew 5.2% organically, strong in UK/Germany laundry but softer volumes in Southern Europe mirroring Unilever's wallet concerns. APAC was flat at 0.8%, offset by India sachet packs despite China softness. Latin America excelled at 12.1%, via Mexico/Brazil local brands like SolFresca.

Free cash flow was $2.4 billion, up 18%, funding $1.2 billion share repurchases and a dividend hike to $0.72 per share—our 47th consecutive increase. Net leverage is 2.1x with $8.5 billion liquidity.

Turning to outlook, for Q4 we expect organic sales growth of 5-7%, pricing 4-6%, volumes flat to +2%. Gross margin to expand 100-150 bps to ~56.5% via Project Horizon robotics and palm traceability. Adjusted EPS $1.72-$1.78, up 10-14%. Full-year: organic sales +7.5-8.5%, EPS $6.45-$6.65, FCF 95%+ of net income. Capex $1.8 billion on DTC and fermentation. Tailwinds in health, e-comm at 18% sales, sustainability with Scope 3 down 15%. Risks: FX, cocoa, but hedged 70%.

Now, turning to our gross margin outlook, a cornerstone of profitability at GCB. For full FY2024, we're guiding consolidated gross margins of 46.0% to 47.0%, about 150-200 bps expansion over FY2023's 44.5%. This follows 220 bps sequential Q3 improvement from our multi-year transformation across snacks, beverages, and personal care.

Key assumptions: Pricing dynamics to add 100-120 bps, as 2023's 7-9% list increases on Heritage Snacks and VitalQuench sustain, though promotional intensity rises to 18-19% in North America versus PepsiCo Frito-Lay and Mondelez Oreo amid softening growth.

COGS inflation assumed at 1-2% YoY, down from 8-10%, with ag commodities easing: cocoa off 20-25% peaks post-El Niño, palm oil/sugar flat to down. Packaging/freight 0-1%, hedged 80%.

Regionally: North America (55% revenue) +250 bps to 49% via premium PlantPower bars +15% YoY, $50M savings from Texas/Ontario DCs. EMEA (25%) flat to +50 bps at 43%, countering Aldi/Lidl private label with local formulas. APAC/LATAM (20%) +200 bps to 45-46% on China e-comm and Brazil VitalQuench.

Productivity targets $250-300M savings, 175 bps accretion: AI demand sensing at 70% factories cuts obsolescence 25%, fill rates 98.5%; sustainable cocoa sourcing -10-15% costs for EU regs; robotic depalletizing 3-4% COGS cuts; divest low-margin detergents +75 bps mix to RTD beverages.

Sensitivities: FX -20-30 bps, downtrading pressures mix; upside if deflation accelerates. This GCB Edge strategy positions us for 50% margins by 2027, ahead of Unilever/Colgate.

Shifting to pricing actions and their sales impact, core to our strategy amid cocoa +25% YTD, palm +15%, private label push. Q3 organic growth 3.8% sequential from Q1's 2.9%, via 5.4% price/mix offsetting 1.6% volume. NPU +5.1% globally, ahead of 4-6%.

Tailored by category: Snacks/Confectionery (32%) 7.2% hikes on SnackJoy yielded 6.8% NPU, 4.5% growth despite 1.2% volume dip; AI engine simulates scenarios, +12% accuracy. Personal Care 7.1% price/mix for 5.9% growth, flat volume on digital coupons. Beverages flat on 4.2% price, 4.3% volume to private labels, pivoting to ELP.

Regions: NA 6.2% NPU, 4.1% growth; EMEA +3.8% pricing, -2.1% volume; LatAm +9.1%; APAC mixed. Margins up 210 bps to 46.2%, trade spend to 22%, price gaps 25-35% over private. H2 4-6% pricing, dynamic e-comm.

Before Q&A, deeper on price elasticity observations, key amid moderating inflation. Blended elasticity -1.15 in Q3, from -1.35 YoY, better than category -1.28. Beverages -0.95 resilient, Snacks -1.42 elastic.

Regions: NA -1.08, EMEA -1.28, APAC -1.05, LatAm -1.22. Drivers: low cross-elasticity -0.25 with private labels via sustainability; inflation ease. Elasticity Hub ML improves predictions 22%, dynamic pricing pilots. FY25 target -1.10 for 5-7% growth, 150 bps margins to 48.5%.

With that financial overview complete, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to discuss marketing, brand performance, and market share trends.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. We saw strong performance in our core brands. Our digital marketing efforts are driving significant engagement, and we are seeing strong results from our VitalQuench campaign.

Diving into market share trends by category and region—a key Q3 highlight. We gained 80 bps value share across core portfolio per Nielsen/IRI, fifth straight quarter, outpacing category in 7 of top 8 SKUs via pricing, innovation, distribution.

By category: Beauty & Personal Care (35% revenue) +120 bps to 18.2%, NovaGlow serums +15% penetration vs Dove/Garnier; mass shampoos +50 bps via shopper marketing. Home Care (25%) +150 bps to 21.5%, EcoShield +3 pts ACV vs Tide Pods, EPA-certified. Snacks/Beverages (28%) +90 bps to 16.8%, CrunchMax +180 bps flavors vs Lay's; functional waters +110 bps. Health & Wellness (12%) +220 bps to 14.3%, VitaBoost gummies converting yogurt eaters.

By region: NA (45%) +110 bps to 24.1%, e-comm 28% Amazon share. Europe (25%) +60 bps to 17.8%, home care +130 bps eco-packaging. LatAm (15%) +140 bps to 13.2%, Brazil bodegas. APAC (10%) +20 bps, China beauty +250 bps. Emerging (5%) +180 bps protein snacks.

Strategic: ShareGuard AI RGM 2.5x ROI promos; 12 new premium products IRR 25%; nearshoring -20% lead times. FY24 +100 bps share target.

Following me, David Patel will provide an update on supply chain initiatives.

David Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to focus on optimizing our supply chain to improve efficiency and reduce costs. We are implementing new technologies and processes to enhance responsiveness to market changes and mitigate disruptions.

To expand on key strategic priorities and progress, our pillars—portfolio optimization, innovation, sustainability, digital, operational excellence—are delivering in this inflationary, post-pandemic CPG world versus private labels and disruptors.

Portfolio: Focus power brands 70% sales; divested canned soups, redeployed $250M to plant proteins +6.8% organic vs category 3.2%; snacks 18.5% share, beverages +2.5 pts; premium mix 45%, margins +210 bps.

Innovation: 2.8% R&D sales, 120 products; VitalFuel shakes $50M Q3, 25% repeat; NA 55%, Europe keto yogurt +15%, EM +22% localized; hit rate 72%.

Sustainability: 35% less virgin plastic, 65% PCR bottles, compostable wrappers; +14% Gen Z loyalty; 92% RSPO palm, Scope 3 -18%; sustainable tea +28% China; +50 bps margins Walmart-linked.

Digital: E-comm 18%, CPG Cloud AI -40% OOS, 92% accuracy; app 5M MAUs +15% basket; omnichannel NA 55%, LATAM 45% Mercado Libre.

Operational: $320M savings 4.2% COGS, EBITDA +180 bps to 22.1%; turns 8.2x, 95% OTD; NA nearshoring 70% Mexico -25% times; India 25% margins.

Summary: Raised FY organic 6-7%, EPS $4.85-4.95, ROIC 18%; outperforming peers in 2-3% growth.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions as before. Our first question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs.

Jane Doe:
Could you provide more insight into the geographic performance, particularly in emerging markets?

Mike Rivera:
Thanks, Jane. Emerging markets were a bright spot, with +180 bps share gains to 8.7%, led by protein snacks in Middle East/Africa urbanization. LatAm +140 bps to 13.2%, Brazil snacks 20% via 5,000 bodegas, inflation-adjusted volumes 98%. APAC +20 bps, China beauty +250 bps K-beauty on Tmall 11% share, India beverages challenged but e-comm 35%. Localized innovation and nearshoring buffered FX, driving double-digit growth in key pockets like India/Brazil sachets and Reliance partnerships, outpacing locals.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Smith with Morgan Stanley.

Bob Smith:
How are you managing inventory levels given the current economic uncertainty?

Sarah Thompson:
Good question, Bob. Inventory turns improved to 8.2x from 7.1x, despite disruptions like Red Sea and avian flu. AI demand sensing at 70% factories cut obsolescence 25%, fill rates 98.5%; Procure-to-Pay digitization $320M savings. Nearshoring 70% US snacks from Mexico -25% lead times, 95% OTD even with cocoa inflation. In uncertainty, zero-based budgeting and 92% forecast accuracy via CPG Cloud keep levels lean, supporting FCF strength without risking service.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alice Johnson with Barclays.

Alice Johnson:
Can you discuss the progress on your sustainability goals and any related cost implications?

David Patel:
Absolutely, Alice. We've achieved 35% reduction in virgin plastic YTD toward 2030 net-zero Scope 1/2, with 65% PCR bottles, compostable snack wrappers—boosting Gen Z NPS +14%. 92% RSPO palm, Scope 3 -18% via audits; precision ag in cocoa -10-15% costs, EU-compliant early. Partnerships like TerraCycle $100M recycling add loyalty, Walmart pricing +50 bps margins. Costs offset by productivity: sustainable sourcing yield tech, qualifying for regs while expanding premium like China tea +28% vs Lipton. Net positive to ROIC.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Lee with Bank of America.

Tom Lee:
What are your expectations for pricing elasticity in the coming quarters?

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Tom. Q3 blended -1.15, improving to better than category -1.28, expect FY25 -1.10. Beverages resilient -0.95 on VitalQuench health halo, snacks elastic -1.42 but managed via flavors. NA -1.08 strongest, EMEA challenged -1.28 but BOGO recoups. APAC/LatAm favorable. Drivers: sustainability differentiation low cross-elasticity, inflation normalization. Elasticity Hub XGBoost +22% accuracy, dynamic pricing pilots +2-3% uplift. Supports 4-6% ASP growth on power brands, value engineering elastic SKUs for 5-7% organic.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Mike Rivera for closing remarks.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions. We remain committed to delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders through our power brands, innovation, and disciplined execution. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
